qns_content.text: Which bacterial shape is correctly matched with its name?

text_solutions: Vibrio is the comma-shaped bacterial form. Coccus is spherical, Bacillus is rod-shaped and Spirillum is spiral-shaped.

qns_content.text: What is meant by alternation of generations in plants?

options.text: Alternation between diploid sporophytic and haploid gametophytic phases
Alternation between sexual and asexual spores in fungi

text_solutions: The plant life cycle has a diploid sporophytic phase and a haploid gametophytic phase that alternate with each other. The duration and independence of these phases vary among different plant groups.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes the general body organisation of fungi?

options.text: Fungal bodies are made only of flagellated cells.
Except for yeasts, fungi are generally filamentous.

text_solutions: With the exception of unicellular yeasts, fungi are generally filamentous. Their bodies consist of thread-like hyphae, and the network formed by these hyphae is called the mycelium.

qns_content.text: What may some bacteria produce under unfavourable conditions?

text_solutions: Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission, but under unfavourable conditions some of them produce spores. These spores help them persist when environmental conditions are unsuitable.

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly describes viral replication?

options.text: Viruses take over the machinery of a host cell to replicate.
Viruses manufacture their own ribosomes outside the host.

text_solutions: Viruses are inert outside their specific host cells. After infecting a living cell, they take over the host-cell machinery to produce new viral particles; therefore, they are obligate parasites.

qns_content.text: What do cyanobacteria often form in polluted water bodies?

text_solutions: Cyanobacterial colonies are generally surrounded by a gelatinous sheath and often form blooms in polluted water bodies. Cyanobacteria may be unicellular, colonial or filamentous.

qns_content.text: In which fungal groups does an intervening dikaryotic stage commonly occur?

text_solutions: In Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes, plasmogamy may not be followed immediately by karyogamy. An intervening dikaryotic stage with two nuclei per cell, written as n + n, occurs and is called the dikaryophase.

qns_content.text: Which asexual spores are formed by Phycomycetes?

text_solutions: Phycomycetes reproduce asexually by motile zoospores or non-motile aplanospores. These spores are produced endogenously within a sporangium.

qns_content.text: Who demonstrated that viruses could be crystallised?

text_solutions: W. M. Stanley demonstrated in 1935 that viruses could be crystallised. The crystals consisted largely of proteins, and viruses were found to remain inert outside their specific host cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following was one of the main criteria used by R. H. Whittaker for the five-kingdom classification?

text_solutions: Whittaker used cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships as the principal criteria for his five-kingdom classification.

qns_content.text: How is a zygospore formed in Phycomycetes?

text_solutions: In Phycomycetes, sexual reproduction results in the formation of a zygospore by the fusion of two gametes. The gametes may be similar in morphology or may differ from each other.

qns_content.text: Which feature is found in some marine amoeboid protozoans?

text_solutions: Amoeboid protozoans move and capture prey by forming pseudopodia. Some marine amoeboid forms also possess silica shells on their surface.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes Albugo?

options.text: It is a ciliated protozoan found in fresh water.
It is a parasitic member of Phycomycetes found on mustard.
It is a basidiomycete that causes wheat rust.
It is a cyanobacterium that fixes nitrogen.

text_solutions: Albugo is a member of Phycomycetes and occurs as a parasitic fungus on mustard. Other examples of this fungal class include Mucor and Rhizopus.

qns_content.text: What is the network of fungal hyphae called?

text_solutions: The fungal body generally consists of long, slender, thread-like structures called hyphae. The network formed by these hyphae is known as the mycelium.

qns_content.text: How do euglenoids behave when deprived of sunlight?

options.text: They behave as heterotrophs and prey on smaller organisms.

text_solutions: Euglenoids are photosynthetic in the presence of sunlight. When sunlight is unavailable, they behave as heterotrophs by preying on smaller organisms.

qns_content.text: How are the two flagella arranged in most dinoflagellates?

options.text: One is longitudinal and the other is transverse.

text_solutions: Most dinoflagellates possess two flagella. One lies longitudinally, while the other lies transversely in a furrow between the stiff cellulose plates of the cell wall.

qns_content.text: Which edible fungi are described as delicacies among Ascomycetes?

text_solutions: Morels and truffles are edible members of Ascomycetes and are regarded as delicacies. Ascomycetes are commonly called sac fungi.

qns_content.text: Which of the following diseases is caused by bacteria?

text_solutions: Citrus canker is listed as a bacterial disease. Malaria is caused by Plasmodium, sleeping sickness is associated with parasitic flagellated protozoans, and wheat rust is caused by Puccinia, a fungus.

qns_content.text: What important ecological role is performed by many Deuteromycetes?

options.text: They act as primary producers in oceans.
They decompose litter and help in mineral cycling.

text_solutions: A large number of Deuteromycetes are decomposers of litter. By breaking down this material, they help return mineral nutrients to the environment and therefore contribute to mineral cycling.

qns_content.text: Which activity of heterotrophic bacteria is directly useful in food production?

text_solutions: Some heterotrophic bacteria are useful in converting milk into curd. Other beneficial roles mentioned for these bacteria include antibiotic production and nitrogen fixation in the roots of legumes.

qns_content.text: Why are the boundaries of Kingdom Protista described as not well defined?

options.text: The same organism may be viewed differently by different biologists.

text_solutions: The limits of Kingdom Protista are not sharply defined because an organism regarded as a photosynthetic protist by one biologist may be considered a plant by another. Protista includes single-celled eukaryotes.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes the ecological importance of diatoms?

options.text: They are the main decomposers of forest litter.
They are the chief producers in the oceans.

text_solutions: Diatoms are photosynthetic chrysophytes and are described as the chief producers in the oceans. Their silica-containing cell walls also accumulate over long periods to form diatomaceous earth.

qns_content.text: What is present on the outer surface of dinoflagellate cells?

options.text: A silica shell made of two overlapping halves

text_solutions: Dinoflagellates possess stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface of the cell. Their colour may appear yellow, green, brown, blue or red depending on the principal pigments present.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes the spores of slime moulds?

options.text: They lack walls and are dispersed through water only.
They possess true walls and are dispersed by air currents.
They germinate only inside a host cell.

text_solutions: Slime-mould spores possess true walls, are extremely resistant and can survive for many years under adverse conditions. They are dispersed by air currents.

qns_content.text: Which set includes only vegetative methods of reproduction in fungi?

text_solutions: Fungi may reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation, fission and budding. Spore formation is classified separately as asexual or sexual reproduction depending on the type of spore produced.

qns_content.text: Which sequence correctly represents the major events of the fungal sexual cycle?

text_solutions: The fungal sexual cycle involves plasmogamy, the fusion of protoplasms; karyogamy, the fusion of nuclei; and meiosis in the zygote, which produces haploid spores.

qns_content.text: Which statement about asexual reproduction in Basidiomycetes is correct?

options.text: Conidia are always produced in large numbers.
Budding is the only mode of reproduction.
Asexual spores are generally absent, but fragmentation is common.

text_solutions: In Basidiomycetes, asexual spores are generally not found. Vegetative reproduction by fragmentation is common, while sexual reproduction ultimately results in the formation of basidiospores.

qns_content.text: Which statement about bacteriophages is correct?

options.text: They infect fungi and usually contain RNA.
They infect bacteria and are usually double-stranded DNA viruses.

text_solutions: Bacteriophages are viruses that infect bacteria. They are usually double-stranded DNA viruses, and their nucleic acid is protected by a protein coat called the capsid.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes the usual genetic material of plant viruses?

options.text: They always contain both RNA and DNA.

text_solutions: Viruses that infect plants generally possess single-stranded RNA as their genetic material. In contrast, animal viruses may contain single- or double-stranded RNA or double-stranded DNA.

What is the main mode of reproduction in bacteria?

text_solutions: Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission. Under unfavourable conditions, some bacteria may also produce spores, and a primitive type of DNA transfer may occur between bacterial cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following groups has cell walls composed of chitin and polysaccharides?

text_solutions: Fungal cell walls are composed of chitin and polysaccharides.

qns_content.text: Bacteria normally reproduce by fission. Under different circumstances, some form spores while others transfer DNA between cells. Which interpretation is correct?

options.text: Spore formation aids survival, while DNA transfer represents a primitive type of sexual reproduction.
Spore formation is the usual method of bacterial multiplication.
DNA transfer produces a multicellular bacterial body.

text_solutions: Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission. Some produce spores under unfavourable conditions, while a primitive type of sexual reproduction may occur through the transfer of DNA from one bacterial cell to another.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of a parasitic protozoan?

text_solutions: Plasmodium is a parasitic sporozoan with an infectious spore-like stage in its life cycle and causes malaria.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a flagellated protozoan?

text_solutions: Trypanosoma is a flagellated protozoan. Members of this group may be free-living or parasitic and possess flagella; parasitic forms can cause diseases such as sleeping sickness.

qns_content.text: Which plant is mentioned as a parasite in Kingdom Plantae?

text_solutions: Cuscuta is mentioned as a parasitic plant. Bladderwort and Venus flytrap are examples of insectivorous plants, which are partially heterotrophic.

qns_content.text: An aquatic microscopic organism floats passively with plankton and possesses two overlapping silica-containing wall layers. Which ecological and economic conclusion follows?

options.text: It is a diatom; it is a chief ocean producer, and its wall deposits form diatomaceous earth.
It is a dinoflagellate; it always produces toxic red tides.
It is a slime mould; it forms fruiting bodies in favourable conditions.
It is a euglenoid; its wall deposits are used for filtration.

text_solutions: Diatoms are photosynthetic plankton and are described as chief producers in oceans. Their silica-containing walls accumulate to form diatomaceous earth, which is used in polishing and the filtration of oils and syrups.

qns_content.text: Why were bacteria and blue-green algae placed together with other plants in earlier classification systems?

options.text: All of them had a membrane-bound nucleus.
All of them possessed a cell wall.

text_solutions: Earlier classifications placed bacteria, blue-green algae and several eukaryotic groups together under plants because all of them possessed cell walls. This approach ignored major differences in cell type, body organisation and mode of nutrition.

text_solutions: Lichens do not grow in polluted areas. Therefore, their absence from a locality can indicate the presence of environmental pollution.

A fungus occurs in aquatic habitats or on decaying wood in moist places, has aseptate coenocytic mycelium and produces asexual spores inside sporangia. Which class and spore types are correctly matched?

text_solutions: Phycomycetes commonly occur in aquatic habitats, on decaying wood in moist places or as plant parasites. Their mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic, and they produce motile zoospores or non-motile aplanospores inside sporangia.

qns_content.text: Which one of the following is true for fungi?
Which statement correctly describes spore formation in Ascomycetes?

text_solutions: In Ascomycetes, asexual spores called conidia are produced exogenously on special mycelium called conidiophores. Their sexual spores, the ascospores, are produced endogenously inside sac-like asci.

qns_content.text: An organism has a cell wall, lacks chlorophyll and obtains dissolved nutrients by absorption from dead organic matter. In which kingdom should it be placed?

text_solutions: The organism belongs to Kingdom Fungi. Fungi are heterotrophic, possess walls containing chitin and other polysaccharides, and absorb soluble organic matter from dead substrates or living hosts.

options.text: Their walls are usually composed of silica plates.

qns_content.text: A composite organism contains an autotrophic partner that prepares food and a fungal partner that provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals. Which observation is most consistent with its identity?

options.text: It is generally absent from polluted areas.
It consists of a fungus and a plant root.

text_solutions: The organism is a lichen. Its algal phycobiont prepares food, while its fungal mycobiont provides shelter and absorbs water and mineral nutrients. Lichens do not grow in polluted areas and therefore indicate air pollution.

qns_content.text: Which fungus is extensively used in biochemical and genetic work?

text_solutions: Neurospora is an ascomycete that is used extensively in biochemical and genetic work. Other examples of Ascomycetes include Aspergillus and Claviceps.

A microorganism is found in the rumen of cattle and contributes to the production of biogas from dung. How should it be classified?

text_solutions: Methanogens are archaebacteria found in marshy habitats and in the gut of ruminants. They produce methane and are responsible for biogas formation from cattle dung.

qns_content.text: A photosynthetic prokaryote contains chlorophyll a, may form colonies surrounded by a gelatinous sheath and sometimes develops heterocysts. Which organism could belong to this group?

text_solutions: The features identify cyanobacteria. Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic prokaryotes containing chlorophyll a. Forms such as Nostoc and Anabaena may fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialised cells called heterocysts.

qns_content.text: A parasitic protozoan possesses an infectious spore-like stage in its life cycle. Which organism and disease are correctly matched?

text_solutions: Sporozoans possess an infectious spore-like stage in their life cycle. Plasmodium, which causes malaria, is the example given for this protozoan group.

A photosynthetic prokaryote contains chlorophyll a, may form blooms in polluted water and sometimes possesses specialised nitrogen-fixing cells. Which group is described?

text_solutions: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic prokaryotes containing chlorophyll a. Their colonies may form blooms in polluted water, and some members fix atmospheric nitrogen in heterocysts.

qns_content.text: Which group of archaebacteria is responsible for methane production from the dung of ruminants?

text_solutions: Methanogens occur in the gut of ruminants such as cows and buffaloes. They are responsible for producing methane, or biogas, from the dung of these animals.

An organism is heterotrophic, has a cell wall and obtains nutrients by absorption. Most members are filamentous, but some are unicellular. In which kingdom should it be placed?

text_solutions: Kingdom Fungi includes absorptive heterotrophs with cell walls. Most fungi are filamentous and multicellular, but yeasts are unicellular exceptions.

qns_content.text: Which organism can multiply rapidly and cause red tides in the sea?

text_solutions: Red dinoflagellates such as Gonyaulax may multiply so rapidly that the sea appears red. Toxins released by these large populations may kill marine animals such as fishes.

qns_content.text: What is the most common ecological role of heterotrophic bacteria?

options.text: They are the chief producers in oceans.

text_solutions: Heterotrophic bacteria are the most abundant bacteria in nature, and the majority function as important decomposers. They obtain food from other organisms or from dead organic matter.

qns_content.text: A prokaryotic colony contains chlorophyll a, is surrounded by a gelatinous sheath and forms a bloom in polluted water. Which further feature may occur in some members?

text_solutions: The organism is a cyanobacterium. Cyanobacterial colonies commonly possess a gelatinous sheath and may form blooms in polluted water. Some forms, such as Nostoc and Anabaena, fix atmospheric nitrogen in heterocysts.

qns_content.text: An infectious agent associated with potato spindle tuber disease is smaller than viruses and lacks a protein coat. What is its chemical nature?

options.text: RNA and DNA enclosed together by a protein coat

text_solutions: The infectious agent is a viroid. Viroids consist of free RNA of low molecular weight and lack the protein coat found in viruses. T. O. Diener discovered them while studying potato spindle tuber disease.

text_solutions: M. W. Beijerinck showed that extract from infected tobacco plants could infect healthy plants. He called the infectious fluid “Contagium vivum fluidum,” meaning infectious living fluid.

Only the asexual and vegetative phases of a fungus are known, and it reproduces by conidia. What should happen if its sexual stage is later discovered?

options.text: It should be moved from Deuteromycetes to the class to which its sexual form belongs.
It should be transferred to Kingdom Protista.
It should be classified as a viroid.

text_solutions: Deuteromycetes include fungi for which only the asexual or vegetative stages are known. When the sexual stage is discovered and its relationship is established, the fungus is moved to the appropriate fungal class, often Ascomycetes or Basidiomycetes.

Bacteria normally reproduce by fission, but two additional observations are made: some form spores during adverse conditions, while others transfer DNA between cells. Which interpretation is correct?

options.text: Spore formation occurs only in photosynthetic bacteria.
Spore formation aids survival, while DNA transfer represents a primitive type of sexual reproduction.

text_solutions: Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission. Under unfavourable conditions, some produce spores, while a primitive type of sexual reproduction may occur through the transfer of DNA from one bacterial cell to another.

qns_content.text: What determines whether a dinoflagellate appears yellow, green, brown, blue or red?

options.text: The number of nuclei in the cell
The main pigments present in its cells

text_solutions: Dinoflagellates may appear yellow, green, brown, blue or red depending on the principal pigments present in their cells. Most members are marine and photosynthetic.

Which group of protozoans moves and captures prey by forming pseudopodia?

text_solutions: Amoeboid protozoans move and capture their prey by extending pseudopodia, or false feet. Amoeba is a common example of this group.

Which fungal group may include coprophilous members that grow on dung?

text_solutions: Ascomycetes may be saprophytic, decomposers, parasitic or coprophilous. Coprophilous fungi grow on dung.

options.text: It divides Monera into two domains and places the eukaryotic kingdoms in a third domain.
It combines all five kingdoms into one domain.
It places viruses in a separate cellular domain.

text_solutions: The three-domain system divides Kingdom Monera into two domains. The remaining eukaryotic kingdoms are placed in the third domain, producing a six-kingdom classification.

qns_content.text: An organism is prokaryotic, photosynthetic and may occur as a unicellular, colonial or filamentous form. Which additional feature would support its identification as a cyanobacterium?

options.text: A protein-rich pellicle instead of a cell wall
Chlorophyll a and a gelatinous sheath around colonies

text_solutions: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic prokaryotes containing chlorophyll a. They may be unicellular, colonial or filamentous, and their colonies are generally surrounded by a gelatinous sheath. Some forms also fix atmospheric nitrogen in heterocysts.
